From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge appliance deploy - ops, BOM & MOP request

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Preferred deployment: private, air-gapped appliance in BioSynth DC (no persistent internet egress).
- Primary goals: low-latency inference for internal LIMS, strict data residency, and offline maintenance windows that align with scheduled QC down-times.
- Procurement is targeting a July delivery window, hardware budget approved pending final BOM.

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) Draft BOM (GPU, CPU, RAM, NVMe, networking) — needed by procurement to finalize PO.
2) MOP (maintenance & upgrade procedure) showing how we perform offline firmware/model updates in an air-gapped environment.
3) Rack/power/weight constraints and any special cabling requirements.
4) SLA/backup strategy and optional on-site support add-ons.

Attachments: I have uploaded the site constraints sheet you mentioned. We'll attach a BOM template and a sample MOP for your team to review.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Vivek: can you produce an initial BOM + MOP draft by EOD Wednesday?
- Tom: please confirm the procurement contact and any additional compliance docs we should include.
- Lauren: I'll loop you in for pricing approval once the BOM is finalized.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: biosynth_site_constraints.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tom Erickson <terickson@biosynth.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge appliance deploy - ops, BOM & MOP request

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for capturing the action items so clearly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement contact: procurement@biosynth.com (cc'd on future threads). Targeting July Po on our side; shipping and customs will be handled by internal supply chain.
- Air-gap constraints: we cannot accept outbound TLS connections from the inference appliance. Offline update process must be possible via sealed USB or signed bundle delivered through courier.
- Maintenance windows: primary QC window is Saturdays 0200–0600 PT; smaller windows are possible for canary updates.
- Rack constraints: 42U bay available; PDUs are 208V single-phase; max weight per rack 1200 lbs; 1U of networking space reserved at top-of-rack.

I'll loop in Priya Natarajan (head of infra ops) once we have the BOM and proposed MOP to schedule a technical walk-through. Priya can verify the power and network details.

Tom
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | BioSynth Labs
[External contact: procurement@biosynth.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Erickson <terickson@biosynth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Edge appliance deploy - ops, BOM & MOP request

Forwarding Tom's reply and site constraints. Vivek — can you take point on the BOM and MOP draft? Please include: 

- BOM: preferred GPU variants (NVIDIA A40 / H100 options), CPU, RAM, NVMe sizing (hot/cold tiers), recommended NICs (10/25/100Gbps options), and redundant PSUs. Use the attached template: biosynth_hw_bom_template.xlsx.
- MOP: step-by-step offline upgrade path (signed bundle ingestion, model install, rollback procedure, KV cache pre-population strategy), test checklist, estimated durations for each step, and validation commands.
- Compliance: include a signed-hash verification step for update bundles to satisfy air-gap controls.

Let me know if you need any details from Tom's team. I put a placeholder in the shared Drive for drafts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3Cxyz_shared-deploy

Thanks — target for first drafts: EOD Wednesday (12 May) so procurement has something to review on Thursday.

Attachments: biosynth_hw_bom_template.xlsx, redwood_mop_sample.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <terickson@biosynth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Edge appliance deploy - ops, BOM & MOP request

Marissa / Team — got it, I'll draft the BOM and MOP. A couple of quick technical clarifications that will change sizing / procedures: 

1) Throughput & model mix: Tom, can you confirm expected concurrency and the largest shading model token length? (e.g., 4–8 concurrent streams of ~1024 tokens vs 20–30 short queries). This will determine whether we recommend H100s or A40s.
2) Quantization & performance: do you expect us to serve fp16/fp32 or run int8/4-bit quantized variants? If quantized, we should include a quality check run in the MOP.
3) Storage retention: how long does the KV cache need to persist across upgrades? If persistent, we'll recommend NVMe hot tier + periodic encrypted backup to an air-gapped tape or secure vault.
4) Signed bundle format: we support signed .tar.gz with an attached SHA256 and signature. Is that acceptable to your security team?

I'll aim to have a BOM (two sizing options) + a draft MOP in the Drive by EOD today. If Tom / Priya can confirm concurrency and quant preference, I'll finalize GPU recommendations.

Vivek
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_mop_sample.pdf]
